# Results — Study 816 (Drawdown Duration)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
**fraction of the trailing year** a name spent **underwater** (its cumulative total return
below its running high-water mark) is a *persistent-drawdown* risk signal; sorting the
cross-section on it should reveal whether the market **pays** for bearing persistent-drawdown
names (a positive high-minus-low spread) or whether they simply **keep sinking** (a negative
spread). Honest sign. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **trailing-252-day time-underwater** — the fraction of the last year its cumulative total-return curve sat **strictly below its running (expanding) high-water mark** — known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the top 30%** (high time-underwater), **short the bottom 30%** (low time-underwater), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled high-vs-low books; a 1,000-permutation two-sided placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. A
drawdown-duration sort is *especially* exposed: the names that spent the most time underwater
and then **de-listed or de-rated** are exactly the ones this panel drops. Any "persistent
losers keep sinking" tilt is therefore *understated* here — the worst offenders survived out.

## The headline — long-high-underwater / short-low-underwater spread

Daily equal-weight top-30% minus bottom-30% time-underwater spread (n = **3,895** days,
median 50 names/day):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long high-UW − short low-UW)** | **−1.12 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **−0.80** |
| one-sample *t* | −0.81 |
| high-UW book / low-UW book | +6.62 bps / +7.75 bps (Welch *t* = −0.41) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | −0.20 |

**Nothing here.** The spread is **−1.12 bps/day** with a Newey-West *t* of **−0.80** —
statistically indistinguishable from zero. The market neither *pays* a discernible premium for
bearing persistent-drawdown names (that would be a significant *positive* spread) nor punishes
them robustly (a significant *negative* one). The faint negative sign — high-underwater names
earned a hair *less* than the names that were making fresh highs — is the whiff of a
distance-from-high / momentum tilt, but it is far too small and noisy to call an edge on this
universe.

## Placebo — is the (tiny) spread even distinguishable from a random sort?

Keep the time-underwater sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted**
panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50), two-sided:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−1.12 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.037 bps (1.007) |
| position of observed | ≈ **1.12σ** from zero — two-sided p = **0.261** |

The observed spread sits barely one standard deviation from the permutation centre: a sort of
this magnitude arises by chance about a quarter of the time. There is no signal to distinguish.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,761) | +0.50 bps | **+0.28** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | −2.46 bps | **−1.17** |

The sign *flips* across the two halves and neither half is significant — a textbook null. The
faint late-era negative is not robust.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | −1.12 bps | 2.14 bps | **−3.26 bps** | −2.34 | −0.59 | −8.2%/yr |
| **5 bps** | −1.12 bps | 10.14 bps | **−11.26 bps** | −8.07 | −2.05 | −28.4%/yr |

The specified book is already slightly negative gross; friction only deepens the hole. Even the
*sign-flipped* book (long low-underwater, i.e. buy the fresh-high names) earns just +1.12 bps/day
gross — less than the 2.14 bps/day round-trip friction at a mere 1 bp one-way. **Mirage** either
way.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent per-name **drift tilt**: with `knob>0` a low-tilt
name drifts down, stays below its high-water mark (high time-underwater) and keeps sinking (low
forward mean) — a planted *negative* high-minus-low relation. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`knob = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.10** (sd 1.15), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** |
| planted (`knob = 0.0010`, seed 816) | **−15.31** (Welch *t* = −14.44) |

The detector recovers a *planted* persistent-drawdown relation cleanly (high-UW names earn
less) and stays near zero on the null (mean +0.10, essentially standard-normal; the 2/20
tail-fires are within binomial noise of the 5% nominal). So the flat real-tape result is a
genuine absence of signal, not a broken sort. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** On 50 liquid US mega-caps the fraction of the trailing year a name spent
  underwater does **not** predict its cross-section of forward returns. The long-high-underwater
  / short-low-underwater spread is **−1.12 bps/day** (NW *t* = **−0.80**), ≈1.12σ from a
  permutation null (two-sided p = 0.26), with a *sign that flips* between eras (+0.28 / −1.17)
  and a clean 20-seed synthetic control. The market neither pays a persistent-drawdown premium
  nor reliably keeps sinking the underwater names — there is simply no edge here. *(Survivorship
  understates any "losers keep sinking" tilt, since the worst offenders de-listed out of the
  panel.)*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The specified book loses money gross (−1.12 bps/day) and net
  (−3.26 bps/day at 1 bp, −11.26 at 5 bps); the sign-flip is eaten by the round-trip friction at
  1 bp. No version pays.
